intro: Settings that cut background work and latency so games and heavy apps get more of the PC: processor and GPU priority, network tweaks, Windows services and scheduled tasks, and visual effects.

System Services.blurb: Windows services you can set to Disabled, Manual or Automatic.
html:
Manual is usually enough

Most services here are recommended at Manual rather than Disabled. A Manual service doesn't start with Windows, but Windows can still start it when an app needs it.

Visual Effects.blurb: Animations, shadows and the other effects from Windows Performance Options.
html:
Presets and single effects

The Visual Effects setting at the top sets every effect below to match the preset you pick. Change a single effect and Visual Effects follows: it shows the preset your choices match, or Custom.

groups.General: Game Mode, mouse acceleration, menu and hover delays, the startup delay for apps, background app permissions, Storage Sense, search scope and System Protection.
groups.Processor: How Windows shares processor time between the app in front and background work, and the priority games get.
groups.Graphics: GPU scheduling and priority, optimizations for windowed and fullscreen games, VRR and Auto HDR, and the display overlay settings that can fix flicker or black screens.
groups.Network: Network throttling, Nagle's algorithm, and the DNS server every network adapter uses.
groups.Security: Virtualization-based security and Memory Integrity. Both protect Windows; turning them off can help game performance at the cost of that protection.
groups.Xbox: Game DVR recording, and the Game Bar's controller button and tips.
groups.Scheduled Tasks: Windows scheduled tasks that collect telemetry and diagnostics or do background upkeep. Turning one off stops it from running.
groups.Accessibility: Keyboard shortcuts that turn on Narrator, Sticky Keys, Filter Keys, Toggle Keys, Mouse Keys and High Contrast. Turn off the ones you don't use so a stray key press can't start them.
